dates.what_en: Employer ended the employment by letter, effective the same day, without notice
Complaint filed with the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (no. AUH-2026-47102)
Employer's written settlement offer: AED 60,000 in three monthly instalments, in full and final settlement
Settlement session at the Ministry (Wednesday); the worker refused the written offer
Ministry referral memo dated; dispute referred to the competent court
First hearing before the labour court (lawyer's handwritten note only)

deadlines.what_en: Pay the worker's wages and all dues within 14 days of the end of the contract on 31 Aug 2026 (Labour Law Article 53); passed without payment

claims.item_en: Unpaid wages for July and August 2026 (2 x AED 22,000)
Unused annual leave, 24 days on the basic wage
End-of-service gratuity (4 years 6 months x 21 days on the basic wage)
Court fees, costs and lawyer's fees

key_facts.fact_en: Monthly salary AED 22,000 in total, of which AED 14,000 basic; the contract sets a 30-day notice period
Wages for July and August 2026 were not paid; the employment ended on 31 Aug 2026 without notice, with 24 days of annual leave unused

Service from 1 Mar 2022 to 31 Aug 2026 is 4 years 6 months, all within the first five years: gratuity 94.5 days x AED 466.67 (14,000 / 30) = AED 44,100; leave 24 x 466.67 = AED 11,200; the four items add up to AED 121,300
The employer admitted the late wages, disputed the notice allowance (saying the termination was agreed), and offered AED 60,000 in writing; the worker refused it on 16 Sep 2026
After the referral the employer offered AED 85,000 orally; the claimant refused (lawyer's handwritten note)
The Ministry referred the dispute to court because settlement failed and the claim exceeds AED 50,000; it found the wages, leave and gratuity due and left the notice allowance to the court

reader_should_flag: The first hearing date (10 Nov 2026) appears only in the claimant's lawyer's handwritten note on the Ministry memo (page 2).
The employer's oral settlement offer of AED 85,000 is recorded only in that handwritten note; the written offer was AED 60,000; the claimant refused both.
Page 1 cites 'البند (9) من المادة (29)' clause first: it is Article 29, clause 9, of the Labour Law (valid).
Page 1 cites 'المادة رقم (51)' with the word رقم: it is Article 51 of the Labour Law (valid).
The employer's 14-day deadline to pay all dues (Article 53) ended on 14 Sep 2026 without payment.
